draft.title: Brain versus heart debate
card: Early thinkers argued over where thought and feeling come from. Some said the heart, and others said the brain.
Aristotle, in ancient Greece, held that the heart was the centre of thought and feeling. He thought the brain cooled the blood.
Others, such as the physician Galen, argued that the brain was the source of thought and feeling. He studied injuries to people and dissected animals.
Over time, evidence from injuries and dissection showed that damage to the head changed thinking and behaviour. The brain came to be accepted as the source of mental processes.
draft.remember: Evidence from injuries and dissection moved the answer from the heart to the brain.

a.q: Which kind of evidence helped settle the debate in favour of the brain?
opts: Head injuries that changed a person's thinking and behaviour
Feelings of the heart racing when a person is afraid
Ancient beliefs that the heart was the centre of the body
Measurements showing the heart pumps blood to the body
a.why: Damage to the head changed thinking and behaviour, which pointed to the brain as the source of mental processes. A racing heart during fear was used to support the heart view, so it did not settle the debate for the brain.
a.clue: Which evidence links damage in one organ to changed thinking?

b.q: A physician in ancient Rome notices that patients with head wounds lose speech, while patients with chest wounds keep speaking normally. Which view does this observation support?
opts: The brain is the source of thought and behaviour
The heart is the source of thought and behaviour
The brain only cools the blood and has no mental role
Thought and feeling come from both organs equally
b.why: Head wounds changed mental function but chest wounds did not, so the evidence points to the brain. It does not support the heart view, because damage near the heart left speech unchanged.
b.clue: Which body part, when damaged, changed mental function?

a.best: Head injuries that changed a person's thinking and behaviour

b.best: The brain is the source of thought and behaviour
